questions.question: Which two languages are official in Canada?
questions.explanation: Canada is officially bilingual, with English and French as official languages.

questions.question: What is code-switching?
options: Switching between languages or dialects depending on the situation
questions.explanation: Code-switching means alternating between languages or dialects, like a Jamaican speaking Standard English at work and Patois at home.

questions.question: Is code-switching a sign of poor language skills?
options: No - it shows mastery of several registers and the ability to adapt
Yes - it means you cannot speak either language properly
Yes - it is forbidden in schools
No - because it only happens in writing
questions.explanation: Code-switching shows that you master several language varieties and can adapt to different situations - the opposite of weakness.

questions.question: What is Jamaican Patois?
options: A Creole language spoken in Jamaica alongside Standard English
questions.explanation: Patois is a Creole language widely spoken in Jamaica, used alongside Standard English in daily life.

questions.question: The Caribbean is best described as:
options: A region of islands where many cultures and languages have met and mixed
A single country with one culture
A region where English is never spoken
questions.explanation: The Caribbean is a region of island nations where African, European, Asian and indigenous cultures have met, creating rich cultural and linguistic diversity.
